real_task: Independently triage psf/requests#7620: determine whether PR 5410's effective change is absent from current main and preserve exact evidence useful to a future maintainer decision.
observed_problem: GitHub labels PR 5410 merged, but a maintainer says it targeted historical master during a branch cutover; the issue remains open and the reporter cannot open a replacement PR.
problem_trace: Official issue 7620, its comments and the Requests Git history.
baseline: Issue metadata and discussion leave three factual questions unresolved locally: exact changed behavior/paths, patch equivalence to current main, and current focused behavior/test coverage.
hypothesis: At most three native read-only inspections can resolve all three questions without a helper, dependency installation or repository modification.
minimum_useful_effect: Reduce unresolved questions from 3 to 0 while preserving exact commit, path and focused-behavior evidence.
quality_control: Pin current Requests main and PR/merge identities; distinguish ancestry from patch equivalence; use the repository's affected source/tests or a dependency-free focused command; make no upstream write or recommendation beyond the evidence.
overhead: Include issue/comment reads, fresh clone, three inspections, trace/reporting, LAB tests, site build, checkpoint refresh and publication.
stop_condition: Stop after three task-specific inspections, on dependency installation, or if current behavior cannot be checked without expanding scope. Do not fork, patch, comment, open a PR or build a history helper.

result.change: remove the #!/usr/bin/env python shebang from a nonexecutable script
unresolved: patch equivalence between PR 5410 and current main
whether current src/requests/certs.py still has the shebang and matching focused coverage

decision_reason: The three-inspection stop fired after two Git retrieval assumptions failed and the final grep targeted the wrong behavior. Preserve the partial external evidence and use at most one direct current-path plus patch-id check in a later gate-permitted evaluation; build no helper.
failures: The fresh clone did not contain merge object f1a94608814a6bdc484233f48b3051dfcb13aa36, so inspection 1 short-circuited before path and ancestry checks.
The remote no longer exposes refs/heads/master, so inspection 2 short-circuited before git cherry.
Inspection 3 learned the PR content only after its current-tree grep had already been written for an unrelated redirect hypothesis.
limitations: The audit did not read current src/requests/certs.py or compute patch-id equivalence after the stop condition. It establishes neither that the old change is absent nor that it is needed. No agent-utility, time, token or LLM-performance claim is made.
